public_rationale: The reported amateur player and 14–1 score are confirmed. The result concerns adversarial play against a leading system, not general superiority at Go.
limitations: The accessible news republication appeared one day after Marcus's post.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: An amateur Go player, Kellin Pelrine, beat a top Go AI system 14 games to 1 in a 15-game series.

statement.excerpt: And the match wasn’t even close; Pelrine beat a top AI system 14 games to 1, in a 15 match series.

our_interpretation: The claim concerns the recently reported series following the late-2022 research, completed before publication.
Top means a leading Go-playing system under ordinary play. It does not mean unbeatable against specially developed attacks.
The score describes the reported set of fifteen games, without assuming a formally organized tournament.
criteria.support_condition: Records or reliable reporting establish that amateur Kellin Pelrine won fourteen and lost one of fifteen games against a leading Go AI.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records establish a different score, a different player, professional status, or an opponent that was not a leading Go system.
